findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Food Handler certificates on file were observed to have been expired. Ensure Food Handler Certificates are renewed every 3 years and maintained on file. New employees should obtain a Food Handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed foods in the market portion of the store stored in boxes on the floor. It appears that extra food is being stored on the floor underneath the relevant display. Food must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. The PIC and inspector discussed using empty cardboard boxes, pallets, milk cartons, or another method. Ensure that all foods are stored 6-inches above the floor by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
**2-103.11 (O) Signed reporting agreement was not available for a new employee that started at the facility earlier this week. Employee health policy was discussed, and owner had employee sign a reporting agreement during the inspection. All other persons working had copies of signed reporting agreements available. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14	Sanitizer solution at front counter was observed soiled. New solution was provided at 200ppm chlorine.
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employee was observed going between glove changes without a handwash. Employee had gloves on while labeling single service container lids and then used an inverted bag over a gloved hand to retrieve raw ground beef for a customer. Gloves were discarded. Hands were not washed prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to then retrieve food from the cold salad case for another customer. Handwashing between tasks and glove changes was discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed prior to donning gloves, when switching between working with raw food and working with ready to eat food, and after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Food thermometer stem was soiled with stuck on food debris and was not used since the day prior. Food thermometer and case were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Pasta salad prepared prior to inspector's arrival was observed in a covered plastic container in the walkin cooler. The surface and internal temperatures were observed at 83F and 105F respectively. Time and temperature during cooling process was not being tracked, but based on information provided the product was still within the first 2hrs of the cooling process. Pasta salad was stirred and container left uncovered to allow for more rapid chilling. The pasta salad was checked about an hour later and observed below 70F. Cooling practices and monitoring the time and temperature during cooling were discussed. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.citation_text:

findings.citation_text:

Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  Bleach solution used for wiping slicer was observed at ~100ppm. The label directions show a required concentration of 150-200ppm. Solution was just prepared recently and not yet used. More bleach was added to bring the solution to proper concentration of 150ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Tray from slicer was washed and rinsed then set aside on a storage rack without being sanitized at the 3 part sink. Owner stated she just emptied the sanitizer solution. A new solution was prepared (100ppm chlorine) to allow for proper sanitizing of food contact surfaces.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 510 - Employee was observed having bare hand contact with baked bread when product was being packaged. Employee was advised to wash hands and put on gloves to wrap the bread. Employee stated he was just about to do that as he grabbed a pair of gloves and went directly back to wrap bread. Owner was advised the employee needed to wash his hands before putting on gloves/between glove changes. Owner discussed handwashing with the employee.

Employees shall properly wash their hands before putting on gloves/between glove changes and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Minimize bare hand contact with ready to eat foods by using proper utensils, deli tissue, and/or gloves when handling/preparing products. Gloves are intended for use and must be discarded when torn, soiled, or an interruption in task occurs.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Potato salad and BBQ pork (both prepared on-site) were observed in the walkin cooler with date marks of 7/8 & 7/6. Owner double checked the calendar used by staff for tracking prep dates of foods made at the facility. Both items were still within the 7 day time frame for use based on the tracking information on the calendar. Removing labels and proper cleaning and sanitizing of equipment were discussed.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket at front counter was at ~10ppm chlorine. Solution was prepared this morning. Sanitizer solution was remade at proper concentration (100-200ppm).

Maintain bleach solution at 100-200ppm, and change solutions every 2-4hr or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.
NOTE: Th bleach will dissolve out of solution over time regardless of use. More frequent use to wipe up food debris and general soil with also break the chemical down at an accelerated rate.
